content.user_title: Explore Codebase Architecture and Data Flow
content.value_statement: Large codebases make ownership, data flow, and service boundaries hard to trace. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Empathy Ledger structure.
actual_capabilities: Maps database domains to the documented type files and key tables.
Explains the Supabase, service layer, API route, and component data flow.
Identifies browser, server SSR, and service role Supabase client locations.
Lists core services and the business purpose of each service file.
Summarizes API route groups for stories, projects, embeds, and admin operations.
Describes tenant filtering and role hierarchy patterns used by the application.
limitations: It is specific to the Empathy Ledger repository layout described in SKILL.md.
It does not verify that referenced files still exist in a later repository version.
It does not replace manual review of security, permissions, or data privacy logic.
It may need updates when services, routes, or database tables are renamed.

use_cases.title: Onboard a New Engineer
use_cases.description: Explain where major domains live and how requests move through the application.

use_cases.title: Plan a Feature Change
use_cases.description: Find likely services, API routes, database tables, and components before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review Data Isolation
use_cases.description: Trace tenant filtering, Supabase client usage, and role hierarchy assumptions during architecture review.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Feature Area
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me where story management lives in this codebase. Include the main types, services, routes, and components.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Data Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how a user action moves from a React component to Supabase for project management.

prompt_templates.title: Map Related Systems
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the files and relationships involved in consent, distribution, revocation, and audit logging.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Tenant Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace tenant isolation for transcript access. Identify tables, route boundaries, services, and role checks to inspect.

output_examples.output: The answer identifies profile lookup, tenant filters, Supabase client choice, and API routes that need inspection.

output_examples.input: How does story distribution connect to consent?
output_examples.output: The answer summarizes the related services, tables, route groups, and compliance logging responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Which files should I inspect before changing project membership?
output_examples.output: The answer lists the relevant type files, organization service, project routes, and membership tables.

best_practices: Ask for file locations and relationships before requesting code changes.
Validate referenced paths against the current repository before relying on them.
Use the data-flow outline to inspect permissions at each boundary.
anti_patterns: Do not assume the reference tables are complete after schema migrations.
Do not use service role paths without checking authorization requirements.
Do not treat generated architecture summaries as a substitute for code review.

faq.question: What repository is this skill designed for?
faq.answer: It is designed for the Empathy Ledger codebase structure described in SKILL.md.

faq.question: Can it make code changes?
faq.answer: The skill guides exploration. Code changes depend on the assistant and user request.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It lists example exploration commands, but the assistant should follow user and tool policies.

faq.question: What architecture areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers database types, Supabase clients, services, API routes, tenant isolation, and role hierarchy.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Empathy Ledger?
faq.answer: It may provide a pattern, but the file paths and domain names are repository specific.

faq.question: What should users verify?
faq.answer: Users should verify file paths, current migrations, authorization checks, and tenant filters in the active branch.
